The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) started as an online satirical movement and sprung to the mainstream as a pressure group in July after forcing the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's then education minister amid massive youth-led demonstrations. Now the CJP movement has Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in its crosshairs. Here is a ten-point breakdown of the controversy surrounding the top election official: The protests concern a contentious, nationwide voter-verification exercise — called the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) — which began last year. Around 130 million names have been removed so far from electoral rolls under the process. Kumar heads the three-member Election Commission of India (ECI) overseeing the SIR process. Last Month, The Indian Express newspaper published a report alleging differences within the ECI over decisions related to the SIR. According to The Indian Express , Kumar's two fellow election commissioners raised at least 14 formal objections over a 10-month period regarding voter registrations, deletions and restorations, as well as control of electoral roll data, but their concerns were allegedly not taken into consideration. The report said that in one objection, one of the commissioners complained that the ECI had acted against the written advice of two commissioners and claimed its action was "unauthorized and illegal." The report sparked a political storm with protests calling for Kumar's resignation, allegedly for undermining the poll body's credibility. The ECI has maintained that all its decisions were lawful, saying that differing views were a routine part of the decision-making process. Kumar is yet to address the allegations against him. Opposition leaders and critics say that those removed from the voter lists include a large number of minority voters. They accuse Modi's BJP party of using the exercise as a tool to secure future electoral gains and question the ECI's independence. The ECI says the SIR removes deceased, relocated and duplicate voters and helps prevent the inclusion of "foreign illegal immigrants." The CJP is not the only group calling for Kumar's resignation.
